Tiger Hunt

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
the real story of Sheba, the Tigris who took a walk on the wild side in Walkerville

Unique Selling Point:
Exclusive television interview with Rassie Erasmus, the owner of Sheba who tracked his tiger for 4 days through neighbouring properties, before ultimately having to make the impossible decision to shoot her.
Exclusive photographs of Sheba and her mate Tyson, as well as videos of the entire search, which turned out to be a hunt.

Summary:
Eight-year-old Bengal tiger Sheba was hand-reared on Rassie's 11.4 hectare plot in Walker Fruit Farms. She had a male companion Tyson. Originally they belonged to his mother. Although he is against the keeping of big cats in captivity, he made her a promise to take care of them when she died.
According to Erasmus Sheba escaped from her enclosure on Wednesday11 January after the electric fence, wire mesh and barbed wire had been cut. Sheba stayed in a catchment camp on the property, where she killed a fallow deer on Friday. She remained there until Saturday.
On Saturday night, he alleged, perpetrators cut the outside fence. On Sunday morning, Sheba escaped into the open. She went on to kill two dogs and a pig, while the police and the local CPF mounted a desperate search.

Between Sunday and Tuesday, Sheba had been near his property in a secluded area of bush where she had water. She returned to the property on Tuesday night for food but evaded capture.
In the early hours of Wednesday 18 January Sheba made her way to a nearby farm, about 3km away from his property, and found herself between a cattle farm and a nursery. The farmer spotted her and alerted the search party. At 2am they started tracking her, until they found her at 3:30am, nearby to 6 houses.

Realising Sheba was about 50m from the cattle kraal, and getting closer to a built up area with children and dogs, Erasmus had to make a decision. Only a vet is allowed to use a dart gun, but the vet was 45 minutes away. Sheba was 80m away, so even if they'd had a dart gun she was out of range. All members of the search party were armed with low calibre guns and Erasmus was worried that they may shoot and only wound her. That would have been even more dangerous.
As a registered marksman Erasmus believed that with his high calibre hunting rifle, he would have the best chance of resolving an impossible situation in the most humane way.
At 3:45am he took aim and shot "his child" cleanly through the head.

Further information:
39 year-old William Mokoena has reported that he was attacked by Sheba on Saturday night.
"It came straight for my throat" he said from his hospital bed, with his left calf bandaged. He had no other visible wounds or scratches on his body. But a photograph taken of Mokoena immediately after the attack show only some bloodstains from minor injuries on his ankle.

Erasmus disputes Mokoena's version and believes the injury is from a dog bite, not a tiger bite and this will be proved in court. He believes a casual labourer who he fired on 11 January for drinking on duty, deliberately cut his fences. This labourer is related to and shares a room with William Mokoena in a nearby commune.

Erasmus is now receiving death threats, and the police have told him to stay away from his farm.
The SPCA have condemned the shooting of Sheba, and are considering whether to lay charges against Erasmus. They were never contacted during the search. They condemn the domestication of exotic pets and are calling for the legislation in Gauteng to be changed.

Script:


SHEBA THE TIGER

Sfx: A tiger has escaped from a property in the Walkerville area south of Johannesburg.

V/O: It was a story that gripped the world’s imagination. An apex predator on the loose, a community living in fear.
A 24-hour track and search operation was launched, led by a police special task force.

Sfx: She’s been spotted here and there but she’s not yet been captured.

V/O: After 4 days of freedom Sheba met a controversial end. Her owner Rassie Erasmus agreed to tell his side of the story.

Sfx: Kon pa se kinders, kom. Kom Sheba, kom. Hey!

Rassie: Sheba was a very playful cat. Sheba was always boisterous and she got up to the most naughtiest things out there. Sheba was the one that would climb trees and she was full of life.

V/O: Sheba and her male companion Tyson lived on this 20-acre property in Walker Fruit Farms for 8 years. Originally they were bought by Rassie’s late mother.

Rassie: From the start I was against it. I was totally against it for various reasons. I mean it’s a heck of a financial impact on your life.

Mac: But you kept them, why?

Rassie: I promised my mom that I would look after them until the day I can’t no more. I haven’t got children of my own, and I looked after these cats like they were my own children.

Rassie: Hello meisie kind, hello pa. Hello my meisie kind!

Rassie: Every morning, they would go into the small enclosure, round about the size of a tennis court. Where they kept at night was massive, about say five, six rugby fields size. I’ve put up double veld span fencing. So two veld span fencing against each other then, plus a welded mesh, plus there was electric fencing, and on the inside we had razor wire as well. They cut though all these fences.

V/O: Rassie believes this was sabotage.

Rassie: The Wednesday night the fences were cut. They went out in one of the catchment camps. I battled to get them back in. Both she and Tyson, got them back in. Thursday night the fences was cut. I put them back in. Friday night the fences were cut again, but in different places. I put them back in again. Saturday night they cut the fences, and then they cut the catchment camp fences and Sheba went out. Tyson was out in the catchment camp. Sheba took a different turn. She went out by the hole of the catchment camp.

V/O: We couldn’t enter the property, as the police advised Rassie to stay away after receiving death threats. This is the boundary fence. The NSPCA’s Douglas Wolhuter says it does not meet requirements.

Douglas: Those fencing specifications did not stand up to be suitable to keep a tiger. It’s quite specific, and the onus rests on the owner because, you know, you're keeping a highly dangerous animal in your possession.

V/O: But Rassie denies this, claiming the enclosure fences were fully compliant.

Within hours of her escape Sheba the tiger had killed a fallow deer and reportedly attacked 39-year-old William Mokoena.

Mokoena: Then it was trying to catch me here on the neck, but I used my feet to fight it off.

V/O: CPF member Gresham Mandy was the first responder to the attack on Mokoena.

Gresham: And then I saw him lying here and I could see just by his legs they were quite bloodied.

V/O: Mandy then took us down to the scene of the attack.

Gresham: The story was he was walking home, he bent down to tie his shoes and then the next thing…

Mac: The tiger was on top of him

Gresham: He felt this weight, and the noise and a heavy animal on top of him.

Flora: He shouted and shouted Sonti, Sonti, here’s that tiger!

V/O: Flora Maseko and her husband were inside and ran to help him.

Flora: When we got there we found him on the ground.
We shone the torches to check around, but there was nothing there.

V/O: But doubt has been cast over this version of events.

Link: This is the spot where William Mokoena was attacked while walking home on the Saturday. And Rassie’s spot is about a kilometer away over there. He says that the bite marks are not the same as that of a tiger.

Rassie: Sheba’s teeth was about that long. I mean the tiger’s teeth is long. The injuries is on the legs. A tiger don’t attack the legs.

V/O: Photos of Mokoena’s injuries show what appears to be a bite mark on the back of his left leg, just above the ankle. There are small puncture wounds on his other leg.

Rassie: I mean there’s no claw marks. Believe me when I’m telling you, if a tiger attacks somebody, that’s going to be the opening and the end of that business.

V/O: Mokoena referred us to his lawyer who declined to discuss the case.

Text: These issues are going to be the subject matter of imminent litigation and thus, it would be a lapse of diplomacy for me to respond thereto at this stage.

V/O: Flora claims the tiger returned in the early hours of the morning.

Mac: What happened to your dog?

Flora: The tiger bit the dog behind the ear.

Mac: So while the tiger is doing this are you guys watching?

Flora: Mmm, we were watching everything happen through the window.

Douglas: Sadly the dog was in such a bad condition that it needed to be euthanized.

V/O: Steven van der Walt is a Peace Officer for Midvaal Municipality.

Steven: There was a lot of concern, due to the fact that we had schools in close proximity. We’ve got livestock all over the place as well. And it was a logistical nightmare for us to search for the tiger because we’re covering such a big area. We all agreed that our first priority is to locate the tiger, then sedate it, and then relocate the tiger. Shooting the tiger was going to be the last, last option.

V/O: That same afternoon Tyson was darted by a vet and relocated to Bloufontein Wildlife Park in Meyerton. Owner Gielie Niewoudt also keeps several big cats, including lions, white tigers and Bengal tigers. Tyson is in a holding camp.
00:04:48
Gielie: He’s been through a lot of trauma, and his female is gone, who he’s lived with for I guess, six or seven years. So it’s a new environment and you must first calm him down. That is the right way to integrate this sort of tiger with other tigers, after he’s had a fair chance to recover.

V/O: Tigers will typically cover 10 to 20 kms during a night’s hunting. Sheba had walked almost 3km west when she was spotted on the Wednesday morning.

Rassie: Around about half-past one in the morning I got the phone call that Sheba was on the farm attacking and killing dogs, and I was told I must come quick.

Douglas: It doesn’t kill to eat it kills because it’s a predator by nature. It’s an apex predator.

Link: The video of Sheba on the prowl was shot from this house just over here. And within this area there’s about 16 people living in different homes, and just over there’s about 60 cattle. One cannot fathom how dangerous the situation was.
01:31:50
Rassie: We could not get hold of any vet, anybody, the head of the CPF, we could not get hold of the police, the captain in charge. All these guys were in the area on standby. Telephonically there was no comms.

V/O: They tracked Sheba around the farm for almost two hours. Rassie called for her as he always did, but Sheba wouldn’t come.

Rassie: The cat outside was a totally different cat. And what I learned to know in the enclosure. It was a total different cat.

V/O: Rassie is a registered marksman and was carrying a high calibre rifle with a telescopic lens.

Rassie: I do not own a dart gun and I’m also not allowed to dart because I’m not a qualified vet.
00:07:13
Douglas: Darting of animals of wildlife can only be done by a vet, and that’s governed in terms of the Veterinary and para-Veterinary Act. No lay person is actually allowed to discharge a dart gun with a high scheduled drug.

Rassie: Our attention was drawn to the back of this quarters. There’s little windows, when we came here some of the workers draw our attention and said to us she was just here.

Sfx: Moo!

Link: Tigers always attack from the back. So can you imagine when you’re a little search party – 3 of you are in waist high bush, covered by trees, looking for an animal that can probably see you, but you can’t see it.

V/O: Eventually at quarter to four in the morning, Sheba appeared on the lawn behind this house. Rassie was standing about 40 metres away behind a tree, faced with an impossible decision.

Rassie: She came here towards the pond. I was out there by the thick tree, there near to the offices. So when I spot her she immediately crouched. I had to make a split-second decision and as hard as it is, I shot her.

Mac: So it happened over here?

Rassie: Ja, after I shot her she slipped into the water. We allowed her to pass on, we pulled her from the water and that’s when all the hell started.

Rassie: Mac, I can’t explain it. It’s like you’re shooting your own child. As much as I love my animals, my biggest fear was her killing a child.

Mac: Who do you, in your mind, blame for Sheba’s death?

Rassie: As far as I’m concerned there’s one person and one person only to be blamed. And that’s the guy who went and cut the fences deliberately.
Without a doubt that’s who I hold responsible.

V/O: But until the keeping of tigers as pets is outlawed, communities remain at risk.

Douglas: I think change is imminent. I think all the role players have seen this is a desperate situation, and if it’s not addressed it’s going to get worse.

Rassie: I do not own a dart gun and I’m also not allowed to dart because I’m not a qualified vet. 00:07:13 Douglas: Darting of animals of wildlife can only be done by a vet, and that’s governed in terms of the Veterinary and para-Veterinary Act. No lay person is actually allowed to discharge a dart gun with a high scheduled drug. Rassie: Our attention was drawn to the back of this quarters. There’s little windows, when we came here some of the workers draw our attention and said to us she was just here. Sfx: Moo! Link: Tigers always attack from the back. So can you imagine when you’re a little search party – 3 of you are in waist high bush, covered by trees, looking for an animal that can probably see you, but you can’t see it. V/O: Eventually at quarter to four in the morning, Sheba appeared on the lawn behind this house. Rassie was standing about 40 metres away behind a tree, faced with an impossible decision. Rassie: She came here towards the pond. I was out there by the thick tree, there near to the offices. So when I spot her she immediately crouched. I had to make a split-second decision and as hard as it is, I shot her. Mac: So it happened over here? Rassie: Ja, after I shot her she slipped into the water. We allowed her to pass on, we pulled her from the water and that’s when all the hell started. Rassie: Mac, I can’t explain it. It’s like you’re shooting your own child. As much as I love my animals, my biggest fear was her killing a child. Mac: Who do you, in your mind, blame for Sheba’s death? Rassie: As far as I’m concerned there’s one person and one person only to be blamed. And that’s the guy who went and cut the fences deliberately. Without a doubt that’s who I hold responsible. V/O: But until the keeping of tigers as pets is outlawed, communities remain at risk. Douglas: I think change is imminent. I think all the role players have seen this is a desperate situation, and if it’s not addressed it’s going to get worse.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): the real story of Sheba, the Tigris who took a walk on the wild side in Walkerville
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Exclusive television interview with Rassie Erasmus, the owner of Sheba who tracked his tiger for 4 days through neighbouring properties, before ultimately having to make the impossible decision to shoot her. Exclusive photographs of Sheba and her mate Tyson, as well as videos of the entire search, which turned out to be a hunt.
metadata.Summary: Eight-year-old Bengal tiger Sheba was hand-reared on Rassie's 11.4 hectare plot in Walker Fruit Farms. She had a male companion Tyson. Originally they belonged to his mother. Although he is against the keeping of big cats in captivity, he made her a promise to take care of them when she died. According to Erasmus Sheba escaped from her enclosure on Wednesday11 January after the electric fence, wire mesh and barbed wire had been cut. Sheba stayed in a catchment camp on the property, where she killed a fallow deer on Friday. She remained there until Saturday. On Saturday night, he alleged, perpetrators cut the outside fence. On Sunday morning, Sheba escaped into the open. She went on to kill two dogs and a pig, while the police and the local CPF mounted a desperate search. Between Sunday and Tuesday, Sheba had been near his property in a secluded area of bush where she had water. She returned to the property on Tuesday night for food but evaded capture. In the early hours of Wednesday 18 January Sheba made her way to a nearby farm, about 3km away from his property, and found herself between a cattle farm and a nursery. The farmer spotted her and alerted the search party. At 2am they started tracking her, until they found her at 3:30am, nearby to 6 houses. Realising Sheba was about 50m from the cattle kraal, and getting closer to a built up area with children and dogs, Erasmus had to make a decision. Only a vet is allowed to use a dart gun, but the vet was 45 minutes away. Sheba was 80m away, so even if they'd had a dart gun she was out of range. All members of the search party were armed with low calibre guns and Erasmus was worried that they may shoot and only wound her. That would have been even more dangerous. As a registered marksman Erasmus believed that with his high calibre hunting rifle, he would have the best chance of resolving an impossible situation in the most humane way. At 3:45am he took aim and shot "his child" cleanly through the head.
metadata.Further information: 39 year-old William Mokoena has reported that he was attacked by Sheba on Saturday night. "It came straight for my throat" he said from his hospital bed, with his left calf bandaged. He had no other visible wounds or scratches on his body. But a photograph taken of Mokoena immediately after the attack show only some bloodstains from minor injuries on his ankle. Erasmus disputes Mokoena's version and believes the injury is from a dog bite, not a tiger bite and this will be proved in court. He believes a casual labourer who he fired on 11 January for drinking on duty, deliberately cut his fences. This labourer is related to and shares a room with William Mokoena in a nearby commune. Erasmus is now receiving death threats, and the police have told him to stay away from his farm. The SPCA have condemned the shooting of Sheba, and are considering whether to lay charges against Erasmus. They were never contacted during the search. They condemn the domestication of exotic pets and are calling for the legislation in Gauteng to be changed.
metadata.Other Footage Sources: Footage provided by Gresham Mandy and Rassie Erasmus
metadata.Reason for legal: Erasmus believes that Mokoena is lying about being attacked by a tiger. The cutting of the fences is a criminal act.
